% ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
% H. Scale, panel and dataset dependence
% ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Dependence on Scale, Panel and Dataset}
\label{subsec:scale}

% FOY:M9.5:1603,1604 ; M10.2:1857,1858 ; M9.4:1551,1552
The symmetric findings do not depend on the scale on which rates are compared (Figure~\ref{fig:estimates_forest}). The symmetric share of the ViT's source gap is $1.101$ on the logit scale and $1.542$ on the ratio scale on CIFAR-10, and $1.026$ and $1.216$ on CIFAR-100; a share above one means that on that scale the directional part narrows the gap. H1 and H2 keep their signs on both scales (Table~\ref{tab:fb4}).

% FOY:M9.5:1603,1604 ; M10.2:1857,1858 ; M9.4:1551,1552
The directional term does depend on scale. On the logit scale the ViT's $\rho$ is $-0.304$ ($[-0.320, -0.289]$) on CIFAR-10 and $-0.413$ ($[-0.546, -0.280]$) on CIFAR-100, and on the ratio scale $-14.66$ and $-14.61$ points. These values are large and negative on both datasets, which makes the ViT the directionally stronger source on the logit scale; on CIFAR-100 this reverses a positive log estimate. The log scale is primary because the quasi-symmetry form $T_{ij} = w_j\simt_{ij}$ is additive on it and because the registration fixed it as primary before any of these runs.

% FOY:M9.5:1605,1606 ; M10.2:1859,1860 ; M9.5:1601 ; M10.2:1846 ; M9.4:1549
The directional term also depends on the panel. Leaving out any one panel member moves $\rho(\cellname{V-scr})$ only between $+0.001$ and $+0.022$ on CIFAR-10, but against the XCiT-S12 as a single-member secondary panel it is $+0.198$ to $+0.204$, and on CIFAR-100 against the XCiT-S12 and the Hendrycks et al.\ model $+0.129$ to $+0.221$. Against a single transformer reference, without an interval, the ViT is a directionally weak source.

For this ViT-Tiny, then, the symmetric dissimilarity holds on both CIFAR datasets and on every scale and panel tested, whereas the directional term is small only on the log scale, against a CNN panel and on CIFAR-10.

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
% I. The conditioning-protocol layer
% ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{The Conditioning-Protocol Layer}
\label{subsec:transfer}

% FOY:TabloIII:159,160,161,162,163 ; M8.4:1195,1196
Everything above uses one conditioning protocol, target-correct, whose rate $r_{\text{cond}} = T_{ij}$ is the quantity decomposed. Because outcomes are logged per image, the same attack runs can be scored under every protocol of Table~\ref{tab:protocol_masks}, and on the pair the choice alone moves the asymmetry from $+4.36\pm0.44$ points under target-correct to $+19.37\pm1.27$ under successful-source, a mean per-pair spread of $15.01\pm0.84$ points (Table~\ref{tab:protocol_settings}, Figure~\ref{fig:protocol_sets}). The direction is positive under all four protocols in all three seed pairs, and also under MI-FGSM (CNN$\rightarrow$ViT $19.07\pm0.33\%$ against ViT$\rightarrow$CNN $15.42\pm0.52\%$, target-correct). The CIFAR-100 and $L_2$ columns of Table~\ref{tab:protocol_settings} show the same spread and sign, and the predictions registered for them are evaluated in Appendix~\ref{app:registrations}.

% FOY:Ozdeslikte kullanilan p:641 ; M8.1:1153,1157,1158,1161,1162
% FOY:Standart egitimli hedeflerde oncul p:868,869,870,871
Most of that range is arithmetic. Equation~\eqref{eq:raw_identity} writes the unconditioned rate as an identity in the target's clean error, the conditioned rate and the premise $p$, the probability that an attack leaves a clean error wrong. Over $36$ off-diagonal directions on adversarially trained targets (two datasets, three seed pairs) the measured $p$ is at least $0.989$ (mean $0.997$) against its upper bound of $1.000$, and the $p = 1$ form reproduces every unconditioned rate to within $0.41$ points. The premise weakens on standard-trained targets, where $p$ falls to $0.877$ and the $p = 1$ form misses by up to $1.58$ points on the clean ViT-Tiny target, the one with the largest clean error; there the general form, Equation~\eqref{eq:general_identity}, with measured $p$ applies.

% FOY:M9.9:1764,1768,1770,1771
Proposition~\ref{prop:hscale} states when a protocol change is harmless for the decomposition: on the scale $h = -\log(1 - T)$, unconditioned and target-correct rates should differ only through a target-side potential. In the pool the test of that statement finds a largest calibration term of $|g| = 0.0044$ (smallest $p = 0.933$). The difference between unconditioned and target-correct source effects is $0.016$ of the target-correct source standard deviation on the $h$ scale, against $0.316$ on the ratio scale and $1.655$ on the logit scale, and the difference in target effects correlates at $1.000$ with the target potential on the $h$ scale. Choosing between these two protocols therefore moves target potentials only, provided rates are compared on the $h$ scale.

% FOY:M8.5:1211,1212
% FOY:Turetilmis:214
The identity does not cover the successful-source and both-correct protocols. Images that the target solves on clean input but the source does not are three to four times more fragile than jointly solved ones ($41.2\pm0.8\%$ and $59.1\pm1.7\%$ fooling against $10.0$ and $18.2\%$), and these marginal subsets differ five-fold in size ($1{,}517\pm102$ against $291\pm16$). Target-correct admits both subsets, whose unequal sizes pull the two directions together; both-correct excludes them, and the directional difference reappears $3.91\pm0.32$ points higher. Successful-source selects on the source's own robustness, which does not follow the clean-accuracy gap, so it contributes a second and partly opposing term.

% FOY:Yayilim-temiz fark:1038,1039,1073,1075 ; RobustBench havuzu:1007
% FOY:M9.4:1567 (S5)
% FOY:RobustBench havuzu:1006,1007 (havuz egimleri; 2026-10-31 tab:external_pool alt blogundan metne tasindi, birlesik.md m17)
% KAYNAK: ON_KAYIT Sec. 5 (S5 bandi +-1.5 puan, tasarim sabiti)
% FOY:Secim kurali B:817
Figure~\ref{fig:spread_clean_gap} places every measured pair on the clean-accuracy gap. The spread over the three protocols that the identity covers rises with the gap (slope $+0.796$, Pearson correlation $r_{\mathrm{P}} = 0.957$ over $60$ pairs) and equals the unconditioned-minus-target-correct difference at $57$ of the $60$ points, where the identity tracks it to within $1.09$ points (mean $0.13$). The four-protocol spread does not follow the gap (slope $+0.092$, $r_{\mathrm{P}} = 0.053$). Within the eight-model pool of Table~\ref{tab:external_pool}, over its $28$ pairs, the three-protocol slope is $+0.872$ (model leave-out bootstrap 95\% interval $[+0.534, +1.274]$, $r_{\mathrm{P}} = 0.944$) and the four-protocol slope $+0.559$ ($[-0.205, +4.582]$, $r_{\mathrm{P}} = 0.350$). Out of sample, the two-by-two pairs deviate from the line by $-0.181$ points on average ($[-0.500, +0.138]$), inside the registered $\pm1.5$-point band (S5). The checkpoint-selection rule moves the four-protocol spread by $-2.16\pm0.93$ points without changing the direction (Appendix~\ref{app:selection}).

% FOY:TabloIII:159,160,161,162,163 ; 185 ; 199 ; Turetilmis:229,230 (SVHN)
SVHN shows what happens when the pair is matched in clean accuracy. With clean gaps of $1.94$ and $1.74$ points in the two seed pairs, the sign of the asymmetry becomes a property of the protocol: target-correct gives $-1.16$ and $-0.85$ points and successful-source $+2.98$ and $+2.41$, while under both-correct the sign-flip permutation $p$ is $0.105$ and TOST accepts equivalence at margins of $\pm1$ to $\pm3$ points. Two seed pairs cannot bound run-to-run variation, so the equivalence rests on the within-run comparison and on the agreement of the two runs. Reported under one protocol only, this pair could crown either architecture as the stronger source.

\subsection{Computational Details}
\label{subsec:computational}

% KAYNAK: CLAUDE.md (Donanim: C1 kampanyasi RTX 5060 Ti 16GB, Q1 ve konsey bloklari RTX 5090 32GB); eski metin 04:638
% KAYNAK: raporlar/konsey_2026-10-29/adeb_eval_pip_freeze.txt satir 156, 234, 266, 269; CLAUDE.md (CUDA 12.8)
% KAYNAK: raporlar/konsey_2026-10-29/10_konteyner_yeniden_kurulum.md satir 276 (commit edilmis imaj adeb_eval:2026-10-30)
% KAYNAK: eski metin 04:638 ve 03:192 (deterministik cuDNN, tohum 42)
% FOY:M10.1:1789,1793,1794,1796
The three CIFAR-10 training pairs of the original cell and their evaluations ran on an NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti (16~GB). The CIFAR-100, SVHN and $L_2$ campaigns, the selection trajectories, the external pool and all registered blocks ran on an RTX 5090 (32~GB). Code ran in a container built on NVIDIA's PyTorch~25.01 image (PyTorch 2.6.0a0, CUDA 12.8) with timm 1.0.27, NumPy 1.26.4 and RobustBench commit \texttt{78fcc9e}, under deterministic cuDNN settings and seed 42. The registered CIFAR-100, ImageNetV2 and gradient blocks reused existing checkpoints and trained no new model. They ran from a committed snapshot of the rebuilt container, with a forked copy of the transfer-matrix script that reproduced the original outputs exactly in a regression run.

% FOY:M9.7:1673
% KAYNAK: eski metin 04:638 (C1 AutoAttack: tam test kumesi, tohumlu 1000'lik parcalar)
AutoAttack used the standard configuration (APGD-CE, APGD-T, FAB-T, Square), on the full test set in seeded 1{,}000-image chunks for the original pair and on the first 1{,}000 test images for the six new models.

% FOY:M8.9:1315,1316
% FOY:M9.1:1452,1453,1454,1455,1456,1457,1470,1485
The three-seed training pipeline of the original pair took 21.7 GPU-hours. The six new runs took 17.79 hours for their clean and adversarial phases, against a pilot projection of 20.47 hours at the 80-epoch cap. Adversarial training stopped early in every run, after 36 to 58 epochs, with selected epochs between 16 and 38. Per-epoch times were 1.05 to 2.19 times those of the pilot, which was measured on an idle GPU. The GPU was at times shared with another process, but the logs do not establish the cause of the slowdown.

\section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
% 5.1 Findings
% ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{What the Measurements Show}
\label{subsec:findings}

% FOY:M10.2:1839
Against a fixed panel of robust ResNet-family CNNs, the adversarially trained ViT-Tiny looks like a weak source mostly because it is unlike the panel, and the unlikeness runs both ways: on CIFAR-10 and the log scale, once each target's white-box vulnerability is divided out, panel examples transfer into the ViT about as poorly as its own examples transfer out. The dissimilarity is present when both architectures are trained from scratch on a matched pipeline, and ImageNet initialization removes more of it for the ViT than for the ResNet. The directional term, the part that would make a model a weak source in its own right, is small and independent of architecture only on the log scale, against the CNN panel and on CIFAR-10. On CIFAR-100 its equivalence is refuted ($+0.143$) while the symmetric share replicates, and on the logit scale it is large and negative, which makes the ViT the directionally stronger source (Section~\ref{subsec:scale}).

The weak-source and dissimilarity readings make different predictions. A source that is weak for its own reasons should gain from a stronger or an architecture-specific attack, yet the gap between ResNet and ViT sources is retained under each source's best attack, and our adaptation of token gradient regularization, not validated against its published gain, transfers worse than PGD-10 from every ViT source (Section~\ref{subsec:attack_side}). Similarity to the target family then accounts for most of a source's transfer deficit into it, in contrast to source-quality effects such as the better transfer of robust surrogates~\cite{awad2025defense}, which the directional term bounds on this panel. For a scratch-trained ViT-Tiny like ours, a black-box score measured with CNN surrogates therefore reflects dissimilarity along with vulnerability, and the surrogate family belongs in the report. The decomposition separates the target-vulnerability and alignment terms of Demontis et al.~\cite{demontis2019adversarial}, while their surrogate-complexity term is split between $r$ and $\log\simt$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:identifiability}(d)), and Section~\ref{subsec:gradcos} links the similarity term to input-gradient alignment as defined by Zhang et al.~\cite{zhang2024why}, an association that leaves the mechanism open.

Whether the scratch-trained dissimilarity persists at ImageNet scale is unknown. On ImageNetV2 the transformers of the two same-recipe pairs initialized from clean models are, descriptively, less similar to the panel, consistent with the registered expectation, while the single scratch-trained pair is uncertain (Section~\ref{subsec:imagenet}). Nor is it known which component carries the dissimilarity, since the contrast changes patch stem, attention and parameter count together. Three behavioral readings that such comparisons invite failed direct measurement (Appendix~\ref{app:behavior}), and Section~\ref{subsec:future} outlines designs for the open questions.

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
% 5.2 Relation to earlier reports
% ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Relation to Earlier Reports}
\label{subsec:prior}

% FOY:M9.9:1706,1708 (r_RV +0.115; potansiyel payi)
% FOY:M9.5:1588
An additive fit with the WideResNet reference places the pair's asymmetry on the source (Section~\ref{subsec:pair_decomposition}). Proposition~\ref{prop:identifiability} explains why two models cannot support that reading. A two-model matrix carries no circulation, and with a single ViT among CNNs the within-family similarity loads onto the ViT's source and target effects, booking dissimilarity as a weak source. Part (b) holds on any additive scale, including the points scale of that fit. The split becomes identified only once the pair is crossed with a fixed panel and each rate is factored into $w$, $\simt$ and $r$, and then most of the ViT's source deficit is symmetric. Within the pair, about half of the log asymmetry is the ViT's higher white-box vulnerability and the rest is a seed-stable directional residual of $+0.115$, above the margin, which belongs to this pair: against the panel the ViT's directional term is equivalent to zero on the log scale.

% FOY:Dis veri Mahmood, Anahtar cift:649
% REF: Dis veri: Mahmood ve ark., Anahtar cift (protokol etkisi -0.59; bc asimetrisi -36.80)
% FOY:M9.2:1497 (V-IN rho ortalamasi negatif; metinde sayisiz)
Mahmood et al.~\cite{mahmood2021robustness} report the opposite direction, as do Benz et al.~\cite{benz2021adversarial} and Shao et al.~\cite{shao2022adversarial}. The conditioning protocol does not explain the disagreement on CIFAR-10: rescored with Equation~\eqref{eq:raw_identity}, their BiT-M-R50x1 and ViT-L-16 pair moves by $-0.59$ points under unconditioned scoring, against a both-correct asymmetry of $-36.80$. Their diagonal reports transfer to an independently trained copy of each model, so $w$ is undefined and the decomposition cannot be applied. Our cells suggest one candidate for the reversal. Their models are pre-trained at scale, and in our design ImageNet initialization both moves the ViT toward the CNN panel and gives it a negative directional term on the log scale, in an exploratory secondary analysis. Whether pre-training, scale or both reverse the direction remains open.

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
% 5.3 Reporting requirements
% ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Reporting Requirements}
\label{subsec:implications}

The four conditioning protocols estimate different quantities, so their distance measures the ambiguity a reader faces when a transfer number arrives without its conditioning set, and that set is the first thing to report (Section~\ref{subsec:transfer}). Unconditioned rates should not serve as architecture comparisons, because their departure from the target-correct rate is the target's clean error entering through the law of total probability (Equation~\eqref{eq:raw_identity}). From published raw rates and clean errors, Equation~\eqref{eq:general_identity} bounds the target-correct rate, and on the scale $h=-\log(1-T)$ the two protocols differ only by a target potential (Proposition~\ref{prop:hscale}). A claim about direction needs the targets' white-box vulnerabilities and a fixed panel over which $w$, $\simt$ and $r$ can be separated, with the scale named, because the sign of the directional term depended on it here (Section~\ref{subsec:findings}). Clean accuracies and the checkpoint-selection rule belong in the same report (Appendix~\ref{app:selection}). Initialization has to be kept apart from architecture: by the interaction of Section~\ref{subsec:twobytwo}, an ImageNet-initialized ViT set against a scratch-trained CNN mixes two effects.

% FOY:TabloI:19
% REF: Tablo I, WRN-28-10 AA 62.76 (RobustBench raporu)
Under the matched mixed-loss recipe the CNN gives the higher absolute robust accuracy under every attack we ran (Section~\ref{subsec:robustness}), yet the WideResNet reference at 62.76\% shows that a larger model trained on extra data with a stronger recipe~\cite{gowal2020uncovering} moves robustness further than the choice between these two families.

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
% 5.4 Limitations
% ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Limitations}
\label{subsec:limitations}

% FOY:M9.4:1553 ; M9.4:1561 (S1 Welch %90 [-0.120, +0.119], sayi metinde IV-D)
% FOY:M11.1:2078 (sonradan uretildi), 2112,2114 (degisen sinama yok)
% FOY:M9.2:1496,1497,1498,1499,1505,1506,1507,1508,1509,1510,1511,1512,1513
Every architectural conclusion rests on two small models, a ResNet-18 and a ViT-Tiny on $32\times32$ images upsampled to $224\times224$, with three runs in the original ViT cell and two in each new cell. Welch intervals, at $1.10$ to $1.95$ degrees of freedom, still place H1 and H2 away from zero but do not support the equivalence of the bridge between the two ResNet-18 pipelines (S1). The binding panel intervals hold the test images fixed; a hierarchical bootstrap that also resamples images, produced after the results were seen, changes no decision, though over three runs per cell it understates the run component. ViT adversarial training depends on pre-training on small datasets~\cite{mo2022adversarial}, and robust transformers have been trained with dedicated recipes~\cite{debenedetti2023light}. The scratch-trained ViT is also the least accurate and most vulnerable model of the design, so a less converged solution and an architectural dissimilarity cannot be told apart; the ImageNet-initialized ViT, close to the ResNet cells in clean accuracy, stays less similar to the panel only in an unregistered comparison (Section~\ref{subsec:twobytwo}).

% FOY:M9.4:1551
% FOY:M9.5:1603,1606
% FOY:M9.2:1497
% FOY:M10.2:1839,1857
% FOY:M10.3:1876,1877,1878
% FOY:M9.9:1759
Beyond its dependence on scale and dataset, the directional term is about $+0.20$ for the scratch ViT against the secondary XCiT panel, and its mean of $-0.118$ in the ImageNet-initialized ViT cell lies outside the margin. Four of the seven CIFAR-10 panel members are ResNet-18 variants; without them no decision changes in an exploratory check (Section~\ref{subsec:twobytwo}), but the panel stays within the ResNet family. The initialization factor bundles pretrained weights, clean-phase length and input normalization, whose separate effects, and their interaction with architecture, are not identified. On CIFAR-100 the ViT's quantities may be confounded with its clean accuracy, which lies below the panel's, and the both-correct sensitivity that would bound this was not produced. TGR ran with its original settings in adapted form, without a check that the adaptation reproduces its published gain on a standard ViT, and attacks with input diversity, more steps or the self-ensemble of Naseer et al.~\cite{naseer2022improving} were not run; step sizes also differ between attacks by design. The simplest law the decomposition suggests, log asymmetry equal to the log vulnerability ratio, failed along the training trajectories ($R^2 = 0.201$ at unit slope) and is not claimed.

% FOY:M10.1:1814 (matristeki modellerde en buyuk fark 0.95, Mo ViT-B; 1.20 yalniz yedek Wong2020Fast, 1816)
% KAYNAK: CLAUDE.md (eps = 8/255)
% KAYNAK: 13_b10_r18_r50_denetimi.md Sec. 6 (R18-R50; sayisiz) ; FOY:M11.3:2202 (log tau sirasi 55/91: medyanin ustu)
% FOY:M11.2:2121 (S10-3 sonradan belirtildi) ; M11.3:2155 (kesifsel)
Our training covers three datasets; ImageNetV2 enters only through independently trained checkpoints, and that panel is descriptive. Its initialized row rests on two pairs of Singh et al.~\cite{singh2023revisiting} and its scratch row on one pair of Liu et al.~\cite{liu2023comprehensive}, counted as scratch-trained on indirect evidence. The ViT-B of Mo et al.~\cite{mo2022adversarial} has a short adversarial schedule and no partner, panel initializations were not verified, and the architectures (convolution-stem ViTs, ConvNeXt, Swin) differ from ours. The common preprocessing departs from some models' own pipeline by at most $0.95$ points of clean accuracy for the models in the matrix, and the distribution shift of ImageNetV2 enters both $w$ and $T$. The gradient cosine is measured at one clean point, and the registered partial statistic removes only additive main effects; the analyses that also control the family split were specified after the results were seen. An energy-weighted cosine can also hide alignment, as one ImageNet ResNet pair with above-median transfer similarity shows (Section~\ref{subsec:gradcos}). Every model is trained under $\Linf$ at $\eps = 8/255$, so the $L_2$ result probes the protocol and not $L_2$ robustness. The mechanism account of the protocol spread is incomplete: the composition of marginal subsets covers three of the four protocols, and the successful-source protocol adds a second driver tied to the source's own robustness. Our leakage ablation, finally, answers a weaker question than the one posed, since split identity and leakage are not separable in its design.

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
% 5.5 Future work
% ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Future Directions}
\label{subsec:future}

A two-by-two design at the next size, ViT-Small against ResNet-50 under one recipe, would show whether the dissimilarity and its response to initialization belong to the families or to these small models (costs in Section~\ref{subsec:computational}). At ImageNet scale, same-recipe pairs trained from scratch would replace the single indirect pair. A cell that applies ImageNet normalization to random weights would separate normalization from pretraining. Measuring gradient alignment along the PGD path and per frequency band would test whether the clean point stands in for the path the attack travels.

% "Its direction comes from the examples crafted on this particular ViT-Tiny"
% cumlesi O1 ile CELISKI oldugu icin kalkti. Kapi G1: "covers three datasets"
% (egitim CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN; ImageNetV2 yalniz bagimsiz modellerle).
\section{Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}

We asked whether an adversarially trained ViT that looks like a weak transfer source against CNNs crafts weaker examples or is simply different from the models it attacks. Measured against a fixed panel of robust CNNs, with the vulnerability of each target taken out, most of ViT-Tiny's source gap on CIFAR-10 is symmetric: the ViT and the CNNs transfer poorly to each other in both directions, and the ViT seeds resemble one another more than they resemble the panel. Trained from scratch on a matched input pipeline and recipe, the ViT is less similar to the panel than the ResNet, a contrast that also carries the ViT's lower clean accuracy; ImageNet initialization removes more of the dissimilarity for the ViT than for the ResNet, and averaged over initialization, architecture leaves the log-scale directional term within the margin. Momentum PGD and our adapted token gradient regularization do not close the gap, and the registered AutoAttack rule flags none of the six new models.

The directional term is small only on the log scale, against a CNN panel and on CIFAR-10. On CIFAR-100 its equivalence is refuted and the ViT is also a directionally weaker source, and on the logit scale it is large and negative, so that there the ViT is the directionally stronger source; the evidence from ImageNet models is descriptive. Input-gradient alignment tracks pairwise similarity on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNetV2; we read it as an association a gradient-alignment account requires, not as a mechanism. Our training covers three datasets, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and SVHN, with ResNet-18 and ViT-Tiny at CIFAR scale; ImageNetV2 enters only through independently trained checkpoints, so whether the pattern holds for larger models trained from scratch at ImageNet scale remains to be measured.

A cross-architecture transfer comparison becomes interpretable when it states its conditioning set, measures each target's vulnerability separately from the similarity between models, does so against models outside the compared pair, and names the scale on which direction is read; Section~\ref{subsec:implications} turns these into reporting requirements.

Input gradients of per-sample losses were measured on $500$ test images per run. Sparsity is scored with Hoyer sparsity, the Gini coefficient and the fraction of components below 1\% of the per-sample maximum, all scale-invariant~\cite{hurley2009comparing}, and spatial locality on the normalized channel-summed energy map (Table~\ref{tab:spatial}). CNN gradients are sparser on all three measures in every run (Table~\ref{tab:gradient}). Paired tests within runs reject the null (Holm $p \leq 2.2\times10^{-12}$), but at the run level, the unit an architectural claim needs, Holm correction leaves $p = 0.108$, so the ordering is reproducible without being significant. Adversarial training produces it: clean-trained, the ViT is the sparser model (Hoyer $0.380$ against $0.347$), and a CIFAR-native ViT is less sparse than the upsampled one. The ViT has the higher absolute alignment (run-level $p = 0.0009$), while signed alignment stays at or below $0.0014$ for both. No spatial descriptor differs at the run level (Holm $p$ from $0.40$ to $0.54$), and two of them change sign across runs, so the sparser CNN gradients are not more localized.

Feature drift is the clean-to-adversarial cosine at each residual block output under the model's own PGD-10 attack ($n = 1{,}000$ per run). In the ViT it is gradual and leaves feature norms within $0.45\%$; in the CNN it concentrates in the first block of the last stage, with a $-13.14\pm1.89\%$ norm change (Table~\ref{tab:feature_degradation}). The CLS token drifts about three times as far as the patch-token mean at their minima, which lie at blocks 11 and 9. The entropy of the head-averaged CLS attention does not change: the largest per-layer change is $0.0045$ nats against clean values of $4.61$ to $5.11$, and run-level TOST at $\pm0.05$ nats accepts equivalence in all $12$ layers (Figure~\ref{fig:feature_degradation}). Attention displacement grows from $0.028$ to $0.084$ with depth, so the attack redirects attention without broadening it. Last-block drift does not separate flipped from unflipped images (run-level $p = 0.20$ for the ViT, $0.080$ for the CNN).

\section{Checkpoint Selection and Sources of Variance}
\label{app:selection}
\label{subsec:selection}

% FOY:M8.7:1269,1273,1274,1286,1287,1293
Varying only how the final checkpoint is chosen from a fixed trajectory (validation split, patience and curve smoothing; eighteen combinations) moves PGD-10 accuracy by $2.62$ to $2.85$ points per seed for the ResNet and $1.58$ to $2.09$ for the ViT. This dispersion is quoted in points and deliberately not as a ratio to seed-level dispersion, because that ratio runs from $0.67$ to $3.38$ (ResNet) and $0.63$ to $7.38$ (ViT) depending on the reference cell. Selection paths can be unstable while outcomes are not: on CIFAR-100 the selected epoch varies by $25$ epochs across ResNet seeds, yet the test PGD-10 standard deviation is $0.32$ points.

% FOY:Secim kuralinin asimetriye etkisi:799,808,813,814,815,816,817,818,825 ; M8.14:1390,1392
At their last checkpoints, twenty epochs after the selected ones, the three training pairs have a clean gap of $10.55\pm0.59$ instead of $12.26\pm0.90$ points and a four-protocol spread of $12.84\pm0.34$ points, with the CNN$\rightarrow$ViT sign kept under every protocol and the identity premise intact ($p \geq 0.9915$).

% FOY:TabloI:16,17 ; TabloIII:159,160,161,162,163 ; M8.8:1295-1309
% FOY:M10.7:2049,2050 (saldiri tohumu SD'si; ilk C1 cifti 1001/2001, ilk 1000 goruntu, 3 saldiri tohumu,
% artefakt alani np.std ddof 0: CNN 0.05, ViT 0.00 puan). 2026-10-31: TODO(foy) kapandi.
The comparisons face four sources of variance. Over three attack seeds on the first $1{,}000$ test images of one seed pair, robust accuracy has a standard deviation of $0.05$ points for the CNN and $0.00$ for the ViT. Training runs move accuracy by a standard deviation of at most $0.55$ points and the transfer asymmetry by $0.23$ to $1.27$ points, depending on the protocol. Within a fixed seed pair the protocol moves the asymmetry by $15.01\pm0.84$ points, and the selection rule moves the spread by about two (Section~\ref{subsec:transfer}). The ratio of protocol to run dispersion is not used as evidence, since with two degrees of freedom its $\chi^2$ interval is very wide.

The third prediction, a deviation of unconditioned from conditioned rates growing with target clean error, gave a positive slope ($+0.656$, $r_{\mathrm{P}} = 0.931$), but two of the three targets have almost equal clean errors ($36.15$ and $36.36\%$), so it is not testable in this design.

The clean-accuracy band for the ViT ($33$ to $40\%$) was missed at $43.17\pm1.10\%$, because the ViT kept $0.885$ of its clean pre-training accuracy under adversarial training against $0.802$ for the ResNet. Both adversarial endpoints fell inside their bands, by $0.22$ points (AutoAttack) and $0.48$ points (PGD-10), margins below the $0.18$ to $1.83$ points by which checkpoint selection moves PGD-10 accuracy on this dataset (Appendix~\ref{subsec:selection}).

The third cannot fail once Equation~\eqref{eq:raw_identity} holds: the fitted slope of $+0.914$ estimates $1 - r_{\text{cond}}$, and we report the slope rather than a correlation, because the eighteen directions take only seven distinct target-error values, and six of the directions share the fixed WideResNet target. The CNN keeps its absolute advantage (McNemar $p \leq 2.729\times10^{-58}$ per seed pair).

% DATA AND CODE AVAILABILITY

\section*{Data and Code Availability}
% 2026-10-02: depo HERKESE ACIK (cnn-vit-robustness-protocols; kurucu betik
% scripts/acik_depo_kur.sh). Kapsam vaatle ayni: analiz kodu + ornek bazinda
% kayitlar + bolme indeksleri + tohumlar; kontrol noktalari (40 GB) istek
% uzerine. Uc yerdeki dil ayni: simdiki zaman, ayni kapsam (burasi, §6, TR).
% 2026-10-31 (konsey turu, brif 12 Sec. 4.1): ImageNetV2, RobustBench
% CIFAR-100 ve ImageNet modelleri, timm ImageNet baslatmalari eklendi; depo
% kapsamina on kayit dosyalari, dondurulmus cozumleme betigi ve hucre
% tablolari eklendi. "about 40 GB" foyde olmadigi icin sayisiz yazildi.
The CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100~\cite{krizhevsky2009learning}, SVHN~\cite{netzer2011reading} and ImageNetV2 MatchedFrequency~\cite{recht2019imagenet} datasets are public. Panel checkpoints come from RobustBench~\cite{croce2021robustbench}, and the ImageNet initializations are the public DeiT-Tiny~\cite{touvron2021training} and ResNet-18 A1~\cite{wightman2021resnet} weights from timm. The analysis pipeline, the scripts behind every table and figure, the per-sample evaluation records, the validation-split indices and the seed lists are public at \url{https://github.com/cagrisahin58/cnn-vit-robustness-protocols}. It also holds the pre-registration documents with their freeze records, the frozen analysis script, the cell tables whose SHA-256 digests the analysis outputs record, and a machine-read copy of Tables~1 and~2 of Mahmood et al.~\cite{mahmood2021robustness} with the scripts that re-score them. Since every protocol and decomposition term is computed from these records, all reported numbers can be reproduced without retraining. Trained checkpoints are available from the authors on request.
